Which is embarrassing, because I’m usually very composed in meetings, I mean, I’ve handled tense rooms before, quarterly reviews, investor calls, all of that, but this is different. It feels like they’re right there.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling unusually high, energized, or irritable lately?\n\nPatient: I don’t know that I’d call it “high.” Energized… I mean, I’m always running at a pretty high level, or I was supposed to be—when you’re the one everyone looks to, you can’t exactly come in flat, right? But unusually? They always talk. Some mornings I get up because there are things to handle, or because I’m already thinking through what has to happen next, but “rested” isn’t really the word I’d use. Some of it I’m just trying to get through what’s in front of me, and then my mind goes somewhere else, and by the time I notice what I’m feeling, the whole morning’s gone.\n\nSo I don’t know if I’d say depressed most of the day. I’m not sure.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem disorganized?\n\nPatient: I don’t… I don’t think people have said it that directly. “Hard to follow” is sort of a subjective thing, isn’t it? Yes… I think so. I used to be the one talking all the time, honestly. In meetings, I’d be the person pushing ideas forward, calling people after openings, following up on every little thing because if you don’t, it all turns into fog.

Yes. I mean… I hate saying it that plainly, but yes.

At work, I’m not really running the division the way I used to. People still look at me like I’m supposed to decide, and I’ll have the file open, the numbers there, and I just don’t make the call.
